notes: Company: mid-market SaaS that builds an automated support/ops agent used by customer success teams.
Primary ask: agentic workflows that perform multi-step tool use: search -> decide -> action (API calls, ticket create, run job).
Latency SLOs: team wants interactive streaming with tail P99 < 250ms for token streaming in happy path; overall end-to-end action latency target ~1.5s for simple ops.

Tool-calling concerns: current prototype suffers from inconsistent tool-call returns and timeouts; need clear retry semantics, idempotency guidance, and a way to surface tool-call failure to user gracefully.
Quote (CTO): "If streaming degrades or function calls timeout, agent must fail fast and surface the step — we can't have silent retries that duplicate actions."
Architecture preference: start on Redwood Hosted API (faster onboarding), then migrate to Dedicated for predictable throughput and VPC connectivity once POC validates patterns.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market; willing to commit to Dedicated if unit economics (tokens / tool-call overhead) are predictable. Ask: batching / cache recommendations to reduce token spend.
Integration notes: they will run tool-call simulators that intentionally delay/return 500s to test fallback policies — want guidance on automatic fallback to safe-mode model variant.
Security: must present audit logs for tool calls and call payloads (redaction ok) for compliance review.
Operational: want per-request tracing (token-level cost + tool-call trace) in Redwood Console to map incidents back to user flows.
POC success metrics (agreed): P99 streaming tail latency <= 250ms, tool-call success rate >= 99% under 100 rps, clear fallback behavior for 5s+ tool latency.
Pre-demo asks: sample template for multi-step agent with tool-call idempotency patterns; recommended timeout/retry defaults; example prompts + eval set.
Local blockers: internal infra team needs 3 weeks to open access for SSO testing; finance expecting pricing from Jordan by 2024-11-20.
Sales notes: emphasize Dedicated sizing and burst options; highlight smart routing and automatic fallback as reliability story.
